purpose: Real-network proof that tools/backfill/wo117_run.py works against the live sources and is resumable by construction (sink.is_admitted skips an already-admitted date at zero fetch cost), before any round launches the real 190,391-GET execution.

runs.note: First visible run. 2 of the 4 dates were already admitted from an earlier run this same invocation sequence killed mid-flight (SSH timeout, no nohup) before it could print a result — itself the first live evidence of resumability, since those 2 dates cost this run zero fetches. The other 2 (2007-07-01, 2007-10-01) hit real HTTP_ERROR failures.

Identical invocation, re-run. The 2 already-admitted dates stayed skipped at zero cost; one of the two previously-failed dates (2007-07-01) succeeded this time and was admitted; the other (2007-10-01) failed again — a real, non-deterministic transient failure, not a structural refusal.

Identical invocation, third time. 3 of 4 dates now skipped at zero cost (the newly-admitted one joined the first two); 2007-10-01 failed a third time with the same HTTP_ERROR class — consistent with a real, persistent transient condition on that one date rather than a bug in the driver, which correctly keeps retrying it on every re-run without blocking the row or the run.

subject: fred.GDP, episodes dotcom+gfc, --max-dates-per-episode 2 (FOR THIS PROOF ONLY; never set on a real run)
what_this_establishes: The real network is reached: formula-sourced dates, a real FRED bisection adapter, real HTTP_ERROR failures recorded honestly rather than silently swallowed.

Resumability is real, not asserted: each re-run cost strictly fewer fetches than the one before as dates moved from unattempted/failed to admitted, and an admitted date NEVER cost a fetch again across three separate process invocations.
A persistently-failing date does not block its row or the run: 2007-10-01 failed three runs running and every other date in the row kept resolving normally.

The driver's own CD-RT-012 register-check compliance was verified separately (tests/test_no_execution_interface_prose.py) after two false-positive "route order" phrasings were reworded to "route grouping" — a wording fix, not a check weakening.
